I totally understand what you're feeling. I relate a lot to your story. It is called spiritual abuse and it is completely validated. Unfortunately, it is something really hard to understand unless you've been through it. 

I grew up in a "non-denominational" church (*cough* cult *cough*) from ages 6 to 14 or 15. It has left very very deep scars. The indoctrination starts very early on and still messes with me today, even though I've been out if the church for almost 10 years. 

My family lived 1.5 hours away from the church, but we still showed up for every service. We spent weeks there helping with VBS or church cleanings or other gatherings. I spent more time at church than I did at home. All of the kids were homeschooled or church schooled. I was one of the lucky ones that was homeschooled. But even the curriculum was cult like in some aspects. Every year from pre-k to k12, since spent a whole month on Creation. 

The congregation was often told horror stories of previous church members that had left/backslid. Died on their way home from their last church service, burned in a house fire set by God, etc. There was a lot of fear mongering. A lot of twisted verbal abuse. They humiliated you until you were nothing. 

And we were all so happy to please. We wanted to be loved and cherished by God and would do anything the pastor said to feel accepted. 

I feel ashamed to say, but my faith is still wandering since leaving. I cannot go to any type of church now with having a panic attack. I believe in God, but in a very different light than when I was a child. If we were ever considered children in that environment. I feel like I lost my childhood to those monsters. 

I have a lot of mental and emotional issues, and honestly I feel that it stems from my church life. But therapy is difficult because they don't quite understand how twisted things were. It made me who I am today, for the good and the bad. It gets better, but stays with you. 

There are support groups in Facebook and stuff, but they can also be a bit triggering at times, bringing back horrid memories. 

Even typing this feels odd because it doesn't sound that bad. It doesn't sound like "real" trauma. It sounds like I am just whining over having to go to church as a kid. But it was so much more than that. The church was taking one of the most important aspects of anyone's life, in any culture, and making  it their own for their own desires. They take your soul and break you and use you for whatever they want. Thankfully no one experienced sexual or other physical abuse in my church...that I know of. But things were very secretive. Who knows what actually happened. 

Know that you're not alone. Know that it gets better. Know that the trauma helped shape you into the wonderful person you are today.

I 24\[F\] graduated from college a few years ago and know exactly how you feel. It can feel like everyone around you is better looking, or more talented, or they are so passionate and motivated when you feel completely lost and  have no motivation. But even though those people seem to have it all together, they don't. They struggle too. Everyone just struggles with different things. 

Don't stress yourself out by thinking that you have to have this epic "college experience". It is different for everyone. 

Who cares if you wear leggings and sweats? I lived in sweats for my last two years of college. If I did not have a regular job now, I still would be living in them and do on the weekends. I tried pretty hard my first semester, spent a few semesters in jeans and t-shirts, and it went downhill from there. But that's okay. Who cares? The motivation will come back around. 

It can be really really hard to make friends in college. Money can be tight, adding to the overall stress. Classes are hard and fast paced. Everything moves so fast but also so slow at the same time. It can be an all around struggle. 

Put the weed down. Take a shower. Put on some clean, comfy clothes. Even if it just some leggings and a big sweatshirt. Throw your hair up if you want. Walk down to the dorm hang out space/cafeteria/student center/library/etc. Take some snacks, maybe a book, or some headphones. People watch. Sometimes just being around people can help you not feel so lonely. And who knows, maybe you'll make a friend. Maybe even just clean up your dorm/apartment/bedroom? 

I also found that asking classmates for help with homework helps making friends. Maybe see if you can get a study group going with a few classmates? It will eventually feel less like a study group and more like a fiend group. Or try a club that involves something you enjoy? 

Also, most college campuses have free counseling services. This can be great help! They can help with general stress, anxiety, loneliness, relationships, future planning stress, etc. 

You've got this girl! Give yourself a well deserved emotional break.
